transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I’m just tired all the time and don’t have the energy to do much of anything anymore, even the stuff I used to enjoy. My wife eventually insisted I get it checked out, so here I am.
How long have you been feeling this way, and is this the first time you've experienced this kind of low energy?

This low, worn-out feeling really settled in about two or three years ago, right after I started phasing into retirement, and it has pretty much stuck with me ever since. I've never experienced anything like this before in my life; it only started once I transitioned out of my full-time job.
During these past two to three years, have you had any periods lasting two months or longer where you felt completely back to your normal self?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all. Once this low, worn-out feeling settled in after my retirement started, it has pretty much stuck with me constantly. I can't remember a single stretch of time over these last couple of years where I felt completely back to my normal self.
Besides the low energy, have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite, or have you been struggling with feelings of worthlessness or hopelessness?

My sleep is pretty bad—I lie awake with my mind spinning about retirement and then wake up around 4 AM, and my appetite is all over the place, where I'll skip meals during the day but mindlessly snack at night. I also feel this constant low, gray cloud hanging over me, constantly worrying that I'm no longer useful or keeping up since I stopped working. It really makes me wonder sometimes what the point of everything is.
When you mention wondering what the point of everything is, have you had any thoughts of ending your life or wishing you were dead?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of ending my life or wishing I was dead. When I catch myself thinking "what's the point," it's really just about feeling a lack of purpose and motivation since I retired, not about wanting to harm myself.

Would you describe this low feeling as a severe, overwhelming depression that significantly limits your daily functioning, or has it been more of a constant, milder heaviness that you've been dragging yourself through?

It is definitely more of a constant, milder heaviness—like a low, gray cloud that has hung over me for over two years rather than a sudden, overwhelming crash. While it isn't completely paralyzing, it's a chronic, exhausting drag that has slowly caused me to let things slide and back out of my usual activities.
Have you found it harder than usual to concentrate, make decisions, or focus on simple daily tasks like reading or watching television?

I haven't really noticed major issues with focusing or making decisions once I actually get into something. My main struggle is just feeling too tired and worn out to even get started on things in the first place.

During these past two to three years, did you ever experience a period of several weeks where this low feeling became much more intense, making it extremely difficult to perform basic daily tasks or care for yourself?
No, I don't think it ever really spiked or got much worse for a few weeks. It has just been a constant, steady level of feeling low and tired day in and day out.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a chronic, mild depressive state (dysthymia) that has persisted for 2 to 3 years since his retirement. He describes a constant, milder heaviness rather than a severe, acute depressive episode. His symptoms include low energy, sleep disturbance (insomnia and early morning awakening), fluctuating appetite, and feelings of uselessness/low self-esteem. He has had no symptom-free periods lasting 2 months or longer, and his symptoms have never spiked to the level of a major depressive episode, fulfilling the criteria for ICD-10 F34.1 (Dysthymia).
